signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical De-risking
signals.text: Strait of Hormuz conflict escalation and a 5.28% Nasdaq drop drive aggressive risk-off flows into the market open — JPY 1W avg +2.026% (n=7) leads G10 outperformance while AUD 1W avg -2.849% (n=4) lags with a 4.875% G10 spread. The 362bp AUD/JPY OIS carry advantage compresses rapidly as equity unwinds override yield differentials. The Sydney/Tokyo open will dictate whether risk sentiment liquidates high-beta cross carry further. Trade bias: Short AUD/JPY into the open; broad risk aversion dominates yield differentials. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open — risk sentiment opening gap. Risk: Sudden de-escalation headlines in the Middle East drive a fast risk-on rebound above 106.00.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Safe-Haven JPY Bid vs Middle East Risk Escalation
signals.text: Iranian foreign minister statements and tanker mine strikes near the Strait of Hormuz escalate safe-haven demand — JPY COT Leveraged Funds net -29.5k (85th percentile) creates short-squeeze risk into the week's open. USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.51, where options markets reflect severe downside hedging demand via a -1.77 25-delta risk reversal (IV 7.5% vs HV30 5.3%, VRP +2.2%). Japan au Jibun Bank Services PMI at 00:30 UTC serves as the immediate regional economic catalyst. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY into the open; safe-haven flows and options put demand threaten a squeeze on JPY shorts. Catalyst: Japan au Jibun Bank Services PMI at 00:30 UTC. Risk: US 10Y yields jump back above 5.00%, reasserting the +268bp USD OIS carry advantage.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Persistently Weak ESI vs Q3 Retail Sales Data Shock
signals.text: NZD Economic Surprise Index at -30.6 (strong negative) underscores severe domestic economic underperformance — NZD/USD closed Friday at 0.5470 with retail positioning heavily tilted at 93% long. A broader risk sell-off reinforces downside pressure, though oversold tech indicators warn of sharp volatility on any data beat. New Zealand Q3 Retail Sales at 21:45 UTC tests whether persistent data misses continue. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/USD; weak domestic macro momentum supports lower lows. Catalyst: New Zealand Q3 Retail Sales release at 21:45 UTC. Risk: Retail Sales beat forecasts (+0.4% core expected), triggering a short-squeeze back toward 0.5550.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Extreme Short COT Positioning vs Flash PMI Event Risk
signals.text: EUR Leveraged Funds net short -105.8k sits at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range — EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.0975, pressed beneath its 20-day SMA (1.1115). Heavy short crowding creates asymmetry for a short-covering bounce if European economic activity displays resilience. Eurozone Flash PMIs at 09:00 UTC represent the key structural catalyst for European growth pricing. Trade bias: Neutral-to-Bullish EUR/USD on short-squeeze potential; extreme COT short positioning limits fresh downside momentum. Catalyst: Eurozone Flash PMI releases at 09:00 UTC. Risk: Composite PMI falls below 49.0, accelerating downside breaks toward 1.0900.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Extreme Retail Short Sentiment vs Heavy Carry Advantage
signals.text: USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.4341 with retail sentiment stretched to 92% short — creating contrarian upside risk as SOFR/CORRA OIS carry (+136bp) favors the US dollar. Extended technical momentum (close above 10-day high) combines with compressed US Thanksgiving week liquidity to raise breakout potential. US CB Consumer Confidence and 5-Year Note Auctions on Tuesday provide near-term macro direction. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; contrarian retail positioning and positive carry support higher spot levels. Catalyst: US CB Consumer Confidence at 15:00 UTC on Tuesday. Risk: WTI crude spikes above $88/bbl on Hormuz supply disruptions, boosting CAD value.
